pages.name: Mirror of −3 − j2
pages.task: What is the conjugate of `−3 − j2`?
pages.why: Keep the real part, `−3`, and flip the sign of the j part, so `−j2` becomes `+j2`. The conjugate is `−3 + j2`, the mirror image of `−3 − j2` in the real axis.

pages.name: On the mirror line
pages.text: A number on the real axis, such as 5, sits on the mirror line. Its j part is 0, and flipping 0 changes nothing, so 5 is its own conjugate.

pages.name: Mirror of 5
pages.why: 5 sits on the real axis, so its j part is 0. Keep the real part, 5, and flip the sign of 0, which is still 0. So the conjugate of 5 is 5 itself.

pages.name: Times its mirror
pages.text: Now multiply `3 + j4` by its mirror `3 − j4` with the four tiles. The two j tiles are the same size with opposite signs, so they cancel. In the last tile `j × j = −1`, so it becomes `+16`, not `−16`. The answer is `9 + 16 = 25`, with no j part at all.

pages.alt: The complex plane, real across and j up, with an arrow from 0 to 3 plus j4. Its mirror image in the real axis is 3 minus j4. Below, z times its mirror is 25, an arrow lying flat on the real line. Drag the tip of z anywhere on the plane.. Length of z by Pythagoras, the square root of 25: 5.

pages.name: (2 + j1)(2 − j1)
pages.why: The tiles are `2 × 2 = 4`, `2 × (−j1) = −j2`, `j1 × 2 = j2` and `j1 × (−j1) = −j × j × 1 = +1`. The two j tiles cancel, so the answer is `4 + 1 = 5`, a plain number.

pages.name: Dividing
pages.text: To work out `10 ÷ (3 + j4)`, multiply the top and the bottom by the bottom's mirror, `3 − j4`. That is multiplying by 1, so the answer does not change. The bottom becomes 25, a plain number.

pages.name: 5 ÷ (1 + j2)
pages.why: The bottom's mirror is `1 − j2`. The top becomes `5 × (1 − j2) = 5 − j10`, and the bottom `1 + 4 = 5`. Divide each part by 5 to get `1 − j2`. Check: `(1 − j2)(1 + j2) = 1 + 4 = 5`, the old top.

pages.name: A top with a j part
pages.text: When the top has a j part too, multiply it by the mirror with the four tiles. For `(7 + j1) ÷ (3 + j4)` the new top is `(7 + j1)(3 − j4) = 25 − j25`.

Below, z times its mirror is 25, an arrow lying flat on the real line. Drag the tip of z anywhere on the plane.. Length of z by Pythagoras, the square root of 25: 5.

pages.name: (5 + j5) ÷ (2 + j1)
pages.why: The mirror is `2 − j1`. The top becomes `(5 + j5)(2 − j1) = 10 − j5 + j10 + 5 = 15 + j5`, and the bottom `4 + 1 = 5`. Divide each part by 5 to get `3 + j1`. Check: `(3 + j1)(2 + j1) = 5 + j5`, the old top.

pages.name: Dividing by j
pages.text: The conjugate of `j` is `−j`. So to work out `1 ÷ j`, multiply the top and the bottom by `−j`. The bottom becomes `j × (−j) = 1`, and the answer is `−j`.

pages.alt: The complex plane, real across and j up, with an arrow from 0 to 1. Dividing by j turns 1 a quarter turn clockwise, to minus j.

pages.name: (−1 + j2)(−1 − j2)
pages.task: The roots from the first lesson are a mirror pair. Work out `(−1 + j2)(−1 − j2)`.
pages.why: The tiles are `(−1) × (−1) = 1`, `(−1) × (−j2) = j2`, `j2 × (−1) = −j2` and `j2 × (−j2) = −j × j × 4 = +4`. The two j tiles cancel, so the answer is `1 + 4 = 5`, flat on the real axis.

pages.name: 25 ÷ (4 − j3)
pages.why: The mirror of `4 − j3` is `4 + j3`. The top becomes `25 × (4 + j3) = 100 + j75`, and the bottom `16 + 9 = 25`. Divide each part by 25 to get `4 + j3`. Check: `(4 + j3)(4 − j3) = 16 + 9 = 25`, the old top.
